dedupe_keys.name: opentepes open generation storage and transmission operation and expansion planning model

description: openTEPES is an open-source decision support model for integrated generation, storage and transmission expansion planning of large-scale power systems over tactical horizons of 5 to 20 years. It was developed at the Instituto de Investigación Tecnológica (IIT) of Universidad Pontificia Comillas, with the motto of simplicity and transparency, to help planners design a decarbonised, reliable and affordable energy system. It sets dynamic investment decisions for generation, storage and networks for electricity, hydrogen and heat across multiple future years, and full documentation covers input data, outputs, the mathematical formulation, installation and the projects that used it. The model is part of the Open Energy Modelling platform for Europe, Africa's open energy system modelling toolbox and the African Energy Modelling Network tools, and provides scripts to exchange data with integrated assessment models. A 2026 Zenodo data set gives openTEPES inputs and results for Kenya's transmission and generation expansion plan to 2030, 2040 and 2050. Coverage is not tied to a place; users supply system data. The code is accessible on GitHub under the GNU AGPL 3.0 at no cost and is very active, with the latest commit in September 2026. Caveats: large cases need a commercial or strong open solver. Simulation uses are integrated capacity expansion with network constraints for national and regional systems. Related records: model-genx and model-switch are comparable planning models.
inputs: storage and network data for multiple future years
